title: Customer KYC Verification for SIM Onboarding
summary: Check digital KYC submissions for new connections: read ID documents, match the live photo, catch duplicates and point-of-sale anomalies, and route doubtful CAFs to the KYC audit team.

seo.title: AI KYC Verification for SIM Onboarding | VipraTech
seo.description: AI checks on digital KYC for new mobile connections: ID extraction, live photo match, duplicate identities and PoS risk patterns, with auditor review.
keywords: point of sale fraud detection telecom

problem.intro: Every new mobile connection must be verified under DoT customer verification instructions, through Aadhaar-based e-KYC or digital KYC with a live photograph and officially valid documents captured at the point of sale. Errors and fraud concentrate where volume is high and checks are thin: blurred or photocopied IDs, a live photo that is not the document holder, the same face behind several identities, and retailers who cut corners.

pain_points.title: CAF audit is sampled and late
pain_points.detail: Manual audit of customer acquisition forms happens after activation and covers only part of the volume.

pain_points.title: Photo and identity mismatches
pain_points.detail: A live photo of someone else, a photo of a photo, or the same face reused under different names slips through visual checks.

pain_points.title: Field and document errors
pain_points.detail: Address mismatches, expired passports for foreign nationals and missing local references for outstation customers create non-compliant CAFs.

pain_points.title: Retailer-level patterns stay hidden
pain_points.detail: Clusters of doubtful activations from one point of sale are hard to see when each CAF is reviewed on its own.

solution.overview: We build a KYC verification layer that checks each digital KYC submission before or shortly after activation. It reads the officially valid document images, extracts name, date of birth, address and document number, masking Aadhaar per UIDAI rules, and checks them against the CAF fields the retailer entered. A face-matching step compares the live photograph with the document photo, and image checks look for screen captures, photocopies and edited images. Across submissions, it looks for the same face or document behind different identities and for unusual patterns by point of sale. Clean submissions pass; those with mismatches or low confidence are queued for the KYC audit team with reasons listed.
capabilities: Extraction from passports, voter ID, driving licences, masked Aadhaar and other officially valid documents
Cross-checks of extracted fields against CAF entries and connection-type rules
Live photo to document photo face match, with checks for photo-of-photo and screen captures
Duplicate detection of faces and document numbers across connections
Point-of-sale risk view showing mismatch and rejection patterns by retailer and distributor
Audit queue with reasons and evidence for each flagged CAF

workflow.title: Receive the submission
workflow.detail: The digital KYC submission arrives from the retailer app with the live photo, document images and CAF data.

workflow.title: Extract document fields
workflow.detail: Document type and fields are extracted, and Aadhaar numbers are masked at ingestion.

workflow.title: Match face and check images
workflow.detail: The live photo is compared with the document photo, and images are checked for tampering or re-capture.

workflow.title: Check CAF and duplicates
workflow.detail: Fields are compared with CAF entries and connection rules, and the face and document are searched against earlier submissions.

workflow.title: Audit flagged CAFs
workflow.detail: Submissions with any failed or low-confidence check go to a KYC auditor, who accepts or rejects them.

workflow.title: Update systems
workflow.detail: Results go to the activation system, and rejections feed the point-of-sale risk view.

human_in_the_loop: KYC auditors decide every flagged CAF, and no connection is deactivated or retailer penalised on the system's output alone. The compliance team reviews point-of-sale risk patterns before taking any action against a retailer or distributor.
integrations: Retailer onboarding and digital KYC app
guardrails: Aadhaar masked at ingestion and never stored in full
Face data used only for verification and duplicate checks, with limited retention
Thresholds agreed with the compliance team and logged
Access logs on every CAF viewed
compliance_notes: Designed to support DoT customer verification instructions for mobile connections; the operator remains responsible for verification decisions.
Aadhaar is handled per UIDAI rules with numbers masked, and face data processing is designed to support DPDP Act 2023 purpose limitation and security safeguards.

faqs.a: Aadhaar numbers are masked at ingestion and never stored in full, in line with UIDAI rules. Where a connection uses Aadhaar e-KYC, we work with the response your e-KYC flow already returns rather than collecting the data again.

faqs.q: Can this replace our CAF audit team?
faqs.a: No. It checks every submission and prioritises the doubtful ones, so auditors spend their time on CAFs that need judgement. Decisions on rejection, deactivation or action against a retailer stay with your team.

faqs.q: How reliable is face matching on low-quality retail photos?
faqs.a: Photo quality at the point of sale varies, so the pipeline scores image quality first and sends poor captures for review instead of forcing a match decision. The pilot reports face match agreement with auditors separately by photo quality.

faqs.q: Can it run in real time inside the retailer app?
faqs.a: Yes, as an API call before activation, or as a post-activation batch if you want to start without changing the retailer flow. Starting in batch lets you tune thresholds before moving checks earlier.
